findings.severity: high at parser boundary; parent selector must block
findings.finding: A number in the target phrase is treated as part of the part name. `Lower clearcoat on roof 2.` returns an edit targeting `roof 2`, without an explicit amount, and uses the default -20-point delta.
findings.evidence: Test `number-not-amount` fails because parse returns kind=edit.
findings.impact: If the parent resolves loose names or falls through instead of requiring one current, exact helper-owned part match, an unrelated part could be selected.

findings.severity: high at parser boundary; parent selector must block
findings.finding: The parser accepts `rooftop decal` as an edit target even when it is only a substring or unrelated phrase, and buildEdit does not compare parsed.part to zone.name.
findings.evidence: Test `part-name-substring` fails; a separate builder case confirms an edit is produced for parsed part `rooftop decal` with zone name `Roof`.
findings.impact: The parent must bind the parsed target to exactly one currently available helper-owned part before enqueueing the edit. The helper itself does not establish target identity.

findings.finding: A signed negative amount fails the unsigned amount regex, then silently falls back to the default. `Lower clearcoat on the roof by -10 points.` becomes a -20-point edit rather than a clarification.
findings.evidence: Test `negative-input` fails because parse returns kind=edit; it reports `amountSpecified=false` and delta=-20.
findings.impact: Malformed explicit quantities should not be interpreted as an omitted amount.

findings.finding: A missing quantity defaults to 20 points. This supports the exact native C07 phrase `Everything is too shiny; lower clearcoat on roof only.` and produces a roof clearcoat delta of -20, but it also means omitted amounts are actionable by default.
findings.evidence: The native C07 wording test passes and reports `amountSpecified=false`.
findings.impact: The parent should preserve the intended default only where its command contract authorizes it.

findings.finding: The parser accepts integer point offsets, rejects relative percent offsets with clarification, and rejects absolute percent targets with a distinct clarification. A 256-point request is accepted and the builder saturates the resulting channel offset at -127.
findings.evidence: Point/sign, relative-percent, absolute-percent, oversized-offset and builder-bound cases are included in the independent contract test.
findings.impact: Builder bounds are effective; accepted oversized requests are saturated rather than rejected.

findings.finding: For valid edits, buildEdit accumulates against the current R/G/B offsets, maps metalness→metal, roughness→rough, clearcoat→clearcoat, returns the complete tuple, clamps each component to [-127,127], and does not mutate the zone. Its edit contains zone_id, spec_shift, and optional expect_name, with no finish, pattern, or color fields.
findings.evidence: Builder mapping, accumulation, both bounds, no-op, malformed-zone, and immutability cases pass.

findings.finding: The pure module can parse the C07 material sentence as a roof clearcoat shift, but it cannot establish that the native app routes the command before decorative finish lookup or queues it through normal edit and Undo handling.
findings.evidence: Baseline report says the live C07 request selected Flame Lapped Clearcoat as a decorative-pattern candidate and did not apply a material change. This review did not run native/browser/MCP integration.
findings.impact: Do not report an end-to-end or native PASS from this module review. Parent integration must retain the protected-parts question and the exact unique current part-selector guard before normal edit queue and Undo.

findings.severity: high at parser boundary; exact target and full-consumption checks required upstream
findings.finding: A post-inspection supplemental set tested unsupported absolute point syntax, dangling numbers, and unconsumed trailing words. All five became edits: `Lower clearcoat on the roof to 40 points.` and `... roof 40 points.` both became part strings containing the quantity with a default -20 delta; `... by 10 points please.`, `... by 10 points from the front.`, and `... by 10 points only.` retained extra words in the parsed part (the first two kept -10).
findings.evidence: Supplemental tests are explicitly marked post-inspection in the test file and report separately as 0/5, leaving the original 25-case fresh result unchanged.
findings.impact: The parent’s exact unique current-part matching should reject these polluted targets. An absolute target or dangling quantity must never silently inherit the default relative amount.
